description: LunarLink Explorers is an independent space technology project team developing LunarLink-DTN, a lunar south-pole mission planning application. Our project uses NASA/JPL SPICE data to explore solar illumination, Earth visibility, and potential communication opportunities at lunar surface locations. We combine scientific computing, Python development, data visualization, and interactive web technologies to support lunar exploration research and education.
summary: LunarLink-DTN is a lunar south-pole mission planning application designed to explore solar illumination and Earth visibility at selected lunar surface locations. Using NASA/JPL SPICE ephemeris and lunar orientation data, the application calculates the apparent positions of the Sun and Earth relative to a local lunar horizon. It identifies periods when the Sun or Earth is geometrically visible and presents the results through an interactive mission-control dashboard. Built with Python, Flask, SpiceyPy, and Plotly, LunarLink-DTN provides visual tools for comparing lunar surface conditions and exploring potential opportunities for solar power generation and direct-to-Earth communication. The project supports preliminary mission planning, space science education, and public understanding of the challenges of operating near the lunar south pole.
details:
LunarLink-DTN is a Python-based lunar mission planning application that analyses the geometric visibility of the Sun and Earth from selected locations on the lunar surface, with a focus on the lunar south pole.

The application uses NASA/JPL SPICE kernels to obtain planetary ephemeris information and lunar orientation data. Its scientific engine calculates apparent celestial positions in a lunar surface reference frame and determines whether the Sun and Earth are above or below the local geometric horizon. The results are presented through a Flask-powered web application with an interactive dashboard, solar analysis, Earth visibility analysis, and visibility-window calculations.

The project aims to help mission planners, researchers, educators, and the public explore factors that influence lunar surface operations. Solar visibility is relevant to preliminary power-generation planning, while Earth visibility helps identify potential geometric opportunities for direct-to-Earth communication.

Technologies used include Python, Flask, SpiceyPy, NumPy, Pandas, Plotly, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Pytest. The application includes automated tests for its API and analysis functionality.

LunarLink-DTN is a preliminary geometry and visualization tool. It does not yet model terrain-obstructed horizons, calculate solar power output, perform communication link-budget analysis, or establish operational communication through a lunar relay network. These are important areas for future development.
